title: Unit 08: Conjunctions, Transitional Devices & Sentence Types
subject: english-10

questions.question: Identify the type of sentence: 'The moon was bright, and we could see our way clearly.'
questions.explanation: Two independent clauses ('The moon was bright' and 'we could see our way clearly') joined by the coordinating conjunction 'and' form a Compound Sentence.

questions.question: Identify the type of conjunction: 'Not only did he arrive late, *but also* he forgot his notes.'
questions.explanation: 'Not only...but also' functions in paired tandem to join parallel grammatical structures, making it a Correlative Conjunction.

questions.question: Identify the type of sentence: 'Although it was raining heavily, they decided to proceed with the match.'
questions.explanation: Consisting of one subordinate dependent clause ('Although it was raining heavily') and one main independent clause ('they decided to proceed with the match'), it is a Complex Sentence.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a coordinating conjunction (FANBOYS)?
questions.explanation: 'Although' is a subordinating conjunction introducing a clause of concession, whereas For, And, Nor, But, Or, Yet, So (FANBOYS) are coordinating conjunctions.

questions.question: Choose the appropriate TRANSITIONAL DEVICE to indicate result/consequence: 'He failed to submit the paperwork on time; ___, his application was rejected.'
questions.explanation: 'Consequently' serves as a causal conjunctive adverb signaling that the rejection was the direct result/consequence of late submission.

questions.question: Identify the type of sentence: 'Seeing the tiger approaching, the hunter climbed up a tall banyan tree.'
questions.explanation: The sentence has only one finite predicate verb ('climbed') with an introductory participial phrase ('Seeing the tiger approaching'), classifying it as a Simple Sentence.

questions.question: Choose the transitional device expressing contrast: 'She studied around the clock; ___, she found the examination paper challenging.'
questions.explanation: 'However' signals a concession or contrast with the preceding proposition.

questions.question: Identify the sentence type by purpose/meaning: 'Please close the front gate when leaving.'
questions.explanation: A sentence that makes a polite request, command, or instruction with an implied subject 'you' is an Imperative Sentence.

questions.question: Identify the sentence type by purpose: 'May the Almighty shower His countless blessings upon you!'
questions.explanation: A sentence that expresses a pious wish, prayer, or benediction is an Optative Sentence.

questions.question: Identify the type of sentence: 'When the siren sounded, the workers evacuated the factory, but the supervisor stayed behind.'
questions.explanation: Contains one dependent clause ('When the siren sounded') and two independent clauses ('the workers evacuated the factory' and 'the supervisor stayed behind') joined by coordinating 'but', creating a Compound-Complex Sentence.

questions.question: Choose the correct correlative pair: 'Neither the teacher ___ the principal attended the meeting.'
questions.explanation: 'Neither' strictly pairs with 'nor' as correlative conjunctions.

questions.question: Choose the transitional device indicating ADDITION of points: 'Reading books expands your worldview; ___, it sharpens analytical reasoning.'
questions.explanation: 'Furthermore' introduces supplementary reinforcing evidence, functioning as an additive transitional device.

questions.question: Identify the subordinating conjunction in: 'You will succeed provided that you stay focused on your goals.'
questions.explanation: 'Provided that' is a complex subordinating conjunction introducing a conditional clause.

questions.question: Identify the type of sentence: 'Do or die.'
questions.explanation: Two imperative independent clauses ('Do' and 'die') connected by coordinating conjunction 'or' form a Compound Sentence.

questions.question: Which transitional device is used to give an EXAMPLE?
questions.explanation: 'For instance' (or 'for example') introduces specific illustrations supporting a general claim.

questions.question: Identify the type of conjunction: 'Scarcely had he reached the platform *when* the express train departed.'
questions.explanation: 'Scarcely...when' functions as a correlative temporal pair showing immediate sequence.

questions.question: Identify the sentence type: 'How magnificent this architectural masterpiece looks under the moonlight!'
questions.explanation: An exclamatory sentence conveys intense wonder or emotion ending with an exclamation mark.

questions.question: Identify the compound sentence among the following:

options.A: He worked tirelessly, yet he failed to secure the top rank.
options.B: Because he was ill, he missed the examination.
options.C: Having finished his breakfast, he went to office.
options.D: I know the gentleman who spoke yesterday.

questions.explanation: Option A joins two coordinate independent clauses with the coordinating conjunction 'yet'.

questions.question: Choose the correct transitional connector for sequence of time: 'First, gather all ingredients. ___, preheat the oven to 180°C.'
questions.explanation: 'Subsequently' (or 'Next') denotes temporal progression in a chronological sequence.

questions.question: Identify the correlative conjunction error: 'He is *both* intelligent *or* diligent.'
questions.explanation: 'Both' pairs exclusively with 'and' ('both intelligent and diligent').

questions.question: Identify the sentence type: 'A student who is disciplined will invariably excel in every walk of life.'
questions.explanation: Contains one relative clause ('who is disciplined') embedded in the principal clause ('A student will invariably excel in every walk of life'), making it a Complex Sentence.

questions.question: Choose the appropriate conjunction: 'Make haste, ___ you will miss the morning assembly.'
questions.explanation: 'Otherwise' (or 'lest/or') conveys the adverse alternative consequence.

questions.question: Identify the type of sentence by structure: 'Life is real! Life is earnest!'
questions.explanation: Each clause has its own independent subject and verb punctuated separately, forming two Simple Sentences.

questions.question: Which word functions as an ADVERSATIVE conjunction expressing contrast?
questions.explanation: 'But' is an adversative coordinating conjunction denoting opposition or contrast between two ideas.

questions.question: Choose the correct transitional device to summarize: '___, we must acknowledge that perseverance is the cornerstone of triumph.'
questions.explanation: 'In conclusion' or 'To sum up' introduces the final concluding summary of an argument.

questions.question: Identify the sentence type: 'Did the principal announce the winter vacation dates?'
questions.explanation: A sentence asking a direct question ending with a question mark is an Interrogative Sentence.

questions.question: Identify the type of conjunction: 'No sooner had she entered the room *than* everyone stood up.'
questions.explanation: 'No sooner...than' is a standard correlative conjunction pair used with past perfect inversion.

questions.question: Identify the sentence type: 'Work hard, and you will pass the board exam.'
questions.explanation: Consists of the imperative clause 'Work hard' joined by 'and' to the clause 'you will pass the board exam', forming a Compound Sentence.

questions.question: Choose the appropriate subordinating conjunction of condition: 'We cannot go for an excursion ___ our parents grant permission.'
questions.explanation: 'Unless' establishes the negative prerequisite condition ('except if our parents grant permission').

questions.question: Identify the sentence type: 'The sun set, the stars appeared, and the night chill deepened.'
questions.explanation: Three coordinate independent clauses linked by comma and coordinating conjunction 'and' constitute a Compound Sentence.
